entities.name: Aryl nitro reduction
observations: The reactant contains an aryl nitro group, Ar–N+(=O)O−, and the product contains the corresponding aryl amine, Ar–NH2.
Net transformation is reduction of an aromatic nitro group to an aniline; it is not heteroaromatic N-oxide deoxygenation.

entities.name: Zn/NH4Cl in MeOH
observations: Closest empirical record uses zinc and ammonium chloride in methanol at 60 °C for nitro-to-aniline reduction, with 85% isolated yield.
Methanol is the solvent; zinc is the reducing reagent, and NH4Cl likely provides proton source or buffering.

entities.name: Nitro-to-aniline evidence
observations: Additional retrieved records involve downstream coupling chemistry and do not provide clean direct evidence for heteroaromatic N-oxide deoxygenation conditions.
